chances.lead: In this model, on current information, each option’s chance of ‘Reach 800 customers’:

most_likely.text: If Olumi's estimates hold, 'Enter multiple European countries' is more likely to achieve 'Reach 800 customers' in this model (about 41%, against about 33% for 'Test one country before broader commitment'); it rests on Olumi's estimate of 'Broader-entry acquisition what-if'.
most_likely.rests_on: Rests on Olumi's reading of the aim, 3 what-ifs and 1 proposed figure; 4 assumptions and 1 condition.

olumi.title: Proposed by Olumi: Concrete interpretation of European expansion for comparison, not an assertion that multiple-country entry is intended. Total investment is treated as a commitment when the option is adopted, not a cash-payment schedule.

rows.text: If Olumi's estimates hold, the chance that 'Enter multiple European countries' meets 'Reach 800 customers', in this model on current information.
rows.rests_on: Rests on Olumi's reading of the aim, 3 what-ifs and 1 proposed figure; 4 assumptions and 1 condition.

rows.aim: Proposed guardrail: churn no higher than 12%

driver.text: about 4% if 'New customers from existing markets' is low, about 97% if it is high: Under 'Enter multiple European countries', the chance of meeting 'Reach 800 customers' moves most with 'New customers from existing markets': these are its chances over the lowest and highest third of that figure's draws.

changes.text: For 'Enter multiple European countries' to meet 'Reach 800 customers' more often than not, 'Broader-entry acquisition what-if' would have to be above about 121 customers/month (between 95.3 and 173 customers/month).

rows.rests_on: Rests on Olumi's reading of the aim, 1 what-if and 1 proposed figure; 4 assumptions.

rows.aim: Proposed guardrail: churn no higher than 12%

driver.text: under 1% if 'New customers from existing markets' is low, about 99% if it is high: Under 'No new European entry during this window', the chance of meeting 'Reach 800 customers' moves most with 'New customers from existing markets': these are its chances over the lowest and highest third of that figure's draws.

assumptions.text: Provisionally read 800 as the total active customer base reached at least once within twelve months, not 800 European customers or a requirement to sustain 800 thereafter.

whose.words: Supplies a testable reading while leaving target scope and deadline open for correction.

assumptions.text: Read 6–12 months as the window for starting European sales. Before entry, incremental European acquisitions are zero; after entry, the selected average acquisition rate and churn what-if apply.

whose.words: The phrase could instead mean deciding, completing setup or achieving meaningful scale in that window. This provisional reading makes timing explicit rather than assuming immediate entry.

concerns.label: Test one country before broader commitment

assumptions.text: Churn means customer-count churn applied to the opening monthly customer base. Existing-market acquisition is held unchanged across options. New customers are added at period end, and one blended churn rate covers all markets.

whose.words: Minimal stock-flow conventions. The brief does not specify revenue churn, cohort behaviour, cannibalisation or management-capacity effects.

assumptions.text: Both expansion designs use the same broad post-entry churn stress range; there is no evidence yet that either design improves or worsens retention. Without entry, the observed 8% is held constant as a scenario assumption.

whose.words: Avoids claiming that a smaller entry automatically protects retention. The current observation is not evidence that future churn will stay constant.

concerns.label: Test one country before broader commitment
No new European entry during this window

assumptions.text: For each proposed country, establish the applicable permissions, tax, data, consumer or sector rules and the cost and time needed to satisfy them before selling. Recording this prerequisite does not mean it is met.

whose.words: Makes the stated country-regulation concern actionable without assuming Europe means the EU or that particular rules apply to this unspecified business.

concerns.label: Test one country before broader commitment

assumptions.text: Test whether the main barrier to reaching 800 is insufficient market access or retention and acquisition economics in the existing market. Expansion could add customers without resolving the underlying growth constraint.

whose.words: A different explanation for the growth gap: the supplied churn rate makes retention material, while evidence that geography is the binding constraint is absent.

concerns.label: No new European entry during this window

assumptions.text: Replace the independent acquisition and investment what-ifs with internally consistent country-and-channel plans; higher spending is not currently linked to higher acquisition in this model.

whose.words: The brief provides no cost-to-acquisition relationship. The ranges enable exploration but cannot establish spending efficiency or a preferred option.

left_out.text: Customer growth and budget compliance do not establish profitability or adequate cash runway. The stated 12% warning is retained, but no probability of making or losing money is calculated.
left_out.why: Prices, gross margins, acquisition costs, operating costs, cash balance and the definition of losing money are missing.
left_out.question: What are revenue and gross margin per customer, acquisition costs, monthly operating costs and available cash—and what calculation makes 12% churn the danger point?

whose.words: Prevents a customer-count model from being read as a financial business case.

left_out.text: The calculation uses an average acquisition rate after entry; it does not model sales ramp, country-specific cohorts, regulatory delays beyond the entry window, or a later scale-up decision.
left_out.why: Country choices, sales channels and an implementation plan have not been supplied. A late entry may need a longer evaluation horizon than the provisional twelve months.
left_out.question: Which countries and channels are under consideration, and how long after entry would a fair test of demand take?

whose.words: Makes the limitations of a monthly aggregate comparison explicit.
